title: Preservation of Scripture
definition: The preservation of Scripture is the truth that God faithfully keeps His Word so His people are not left without His true testimony.
summary: God preserves His Word so His people can continue to hear, trust, teach, and obey what He has spoken.
christFocus: Jesus taught that Scripture cannot be broken and that God's Word endures, giving believers confidence that His promises remain sure.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
The preservation of Scripture teaches that the God who gave His Word has also faithfully guarded its witness. God's truth does not depend on human strength alone. The Lord has preserved His Word so that His people may know Him, proclaim the Gospel, and walk in obedience.

This doctrine does not deny the history of manuscripts, copying, translation, or study. Rather, it confesses that God's providence has not failed His church.

Because God's Word endures, the church can continue reading, teaching, preaching, translating, and obeying Scripture with confidence.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Some people fear that God's Word has been lost, corrupted beyond use, or made unreliable by history. The preservation of Scripture gives assurance that God has not abandoned His people.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Receive Scripture with confidence and gratitude. Do not treat the Bible as fragile or powerless. Read it, teach it, share it, and build your life on it.
